submission.name: SafeStep
submission.tagline: A camera checkpoint that helps makerspaces catch missing protective gear before a job starts.
submission.inspiration: We wanted to make PPE checks easier in shared fabrication rooms where students move between tasks and supervisors cannot watch every entrance. A quick visual check felt more practical than relying on everyone to remember the full gear list each time.
submission.what_it_does: A member scans an RFID badge or enters a PIN, then stands at the checkpoint camera. The prototype checks for required gear and shows what it thinks is missing; staff can review recent entries and basic compliance trends in a dashboard. It also reads a short spoken reminder when someone needs to add equipment.
submission.how_we_built_it: A React and TypeScript dashboard talks to a Node.js server that stores profiles, room rules, and check-in logs in MongoDB. A local Flask service uses OpenCV and a YOLO model to inspect camera frames, while Gemini turns detected items into a plain-language prompt. We added ElevenLabs speech for that reminder and a small BNY-oriented view of check-in records as a workflow example for organizations managing risk.
submission.challenges_we_ran_into: Getting the camera service, server, and live dashboard to agree on each scan took time, and detection was inconsistent with poor lighting or gear partly out of frame. The end-to-end flow works in our demo, but the model can miss items and the records are not a substitute for an actual safety inspection.
submission.accomplishments: We connected badge and PIN input to a camera check and a saved entry log. We are proud that the prototype can give a specific spoken reminder instead of only showing a generic pass or fail.
submission.what_we_learned: We learned how much coordination a small real-time system needs across Python vision code, a Node server, and a React screen. Gemini helped us prototype explanations, and we learned to treat those explanations as interface text rather than proof that a detection is correct.
submission.whats_next: We would test the detector with more gear types and varied workshop lighting, then add a staff review flow for uncertain scans. A standalone kiosk and a more useful audit export would also make the concept easier to try in a real makerspace.
